Subject: SLA exception request: nightly async inference finalization window

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the throughput. We're close to signing but have a blocker from our ops/procurement teams around the SLA for nightly bulk inference jobs. Our current pipeline sends a nightly batch of ~8–12M records to Redwood for async inference (retail catalog enrichments). The business requirement is that results be "finalized" and landed in our data lake within 12 hours of submission.

Operational reality: we have frequent spikes and occasionally replays; our infra team needs clear guidance on idempotency and retries so we don't double-count or mis-apply enrichments. Procurement asked whether you can accept a contractual exception: allow a 36-hour finalization window for batches >5M with defined retry/idempotency guarantees and monitoring hooks.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide: 
- an exception to the 12-hour window for large nightly jobs (proposed 36 hours),
- a safe-retry policy and idempotency key behavior that we can operate against, and
- visibility into late-job metrics and a remediation/credit plan?

If possible, please send a short write-up we can attach to our SOW and get legal sign-off.

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan — appreciate the clarity and the numbers. Short answer: yes, we can support an exception for large-nightly batches but there are a few guardrails we need to agree on so we keep predictable economics and correctness.

I've attached a draft "SLA exception" doc for your SOW that codifies the proposal. High level:
- Exception window: 36 hours finalization for any single batch > 5M items; standard 12-hour SLA still applies for smaller batches and interactive calls.
- Safe-retry behavior: Redwood will accept idempotency keys (user-provided) for up to 7 days and will dedupe on first-seen key for the job TTL; we will expose a per-job status endpoint.
- Retry/backoff: recommended exponential backoff with max 5 retries; Redwood will implement safe-at-least-once delivery with dedupe to avoid double-applying enrichments.
- Monitoring & credits: we will surface late-job alerts to a webhook + provide SLA credits for >5% of nightly jobs missing the 36-hour window in a monthly period.

Next steps: Karthik can confirm the dedupe/kv TTL semantics and any limits; Evelyn will confirm commercial credit thresholds and contractual wording. If this all looks good, I'll circulate the final PDF and a DocuSign link.

Attaching: SLA-exception-draft.pdf (outline), retry-dedupe-spec.md (technical summary).

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: SLA exception request: nightly async inference finalization window

Marissa / Evelyn — quick tech assessment below; Jordan, copying for transparency.

Notes on implementation and risk:
- Idempotency keys: support a user-supplied idempotency token scoped to a job-id; we'll keep a hash table (KV) for 7 days by default. TTL can be extended for an additional fee.
- Dedupe semantics: first-write wins for the job; if a request replays with the same idempotency key, we return the original job result or job status URI. This prevents double processing.
- Safe-retry & backoff: we recommend clients use exponential backoff (initial 1s, 2s, 4s...) up to 5 attempts. On our side, we will queue retries but mark job attempts in the audit log.
- Large-batch behaviour: for >5M items we shard jobs across workers; partial shard failures can delay finalization — we can parallelize retries per shard. We estimate that under normal load a 36-hour window is sufficient; during cross-region incidents we may exceed that and leverage fallback model variants to keep latency down.
- Observability: we'll add a per-job timeline (submitted -> shards completed -> finalize) and push SLA-late events to a customer webhook or to your SRE PagerDuty integration.

Open questions:
1) Do you need strict exactly-once semantics downstream (we currently provide at-least-once with dedupe tooling)?
2) What SLIs do you want surfaced in the monthlies (p95 finalization time, % jobs >36h, retry counts)?

If Jordan confirms exactly-once is required, that's a larger engineering and data-pipeline change (we can propose a migration pattern).

-Karthik
